title: Anthropic Criticized For Adding Watermarks to Text that Claude Generates - or Processes - Slashdot

content_html:
This week Anthropic announced its Claude chatbot will watermark the text it generates, reports the blog Futurism. "It works by making subtle changes in the AI's word choices across the text it generates, which are supposed to be imperceptible to a human but, in aggregate, form a pattern that is detectable with the tool." Anthropic said it was implementing the watermark system in response to the European Union's landmark AI Act passed in 2024, which requires that AI companies mark content that's been generated or edited by their systems.
TechCrunch notes that other companies including Google, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI, and Synthesia have committed to adhering to the EU's code. But "The news about Claude watermarking kicked off a firestorm on X," reports Forbes, "with users panicking that AI-assisted writing will now bear a kind of permanent 'scarlet letter.'" (Forbes wonders if media companies are normalizing AI "while at the same time stigmatizing the output.")

But there's another issue. Anthropic said the watermark indicates Claude processed text, Business Insider points out, "not that it was necessarily the original author. The company said marks can remain after Claude proofreads, translates, summarizes, or otherwise edits content... a watermark shows that Claude processed text, not necessarily that it wrote it."

In the days since, "Dozens of people have posted on X since Monday that they had canceled their Claude subscriptions, citing the watermark." Vladislav Rajtmajer, a freelance developer in the Czech Republic, told Business Insider he canceled his Claude Max subscription on Tuesday, citing the watermark as the main reason. He said he uses AI for code reviews and translations, and worried an AI label on code shipped to clients could raise questions about authorship or trigger contract penalties... Richard Echols, an AI consultant in Georgia, also said he canceled his Claude Max subscription on Wednesday and that the watermark was a major factor in his decision. He said he uses Claude to create documentation for businesses and worried the mark could appear when he had written the underlying material himself and used the chatbot only for edits. "Even if you edit your own work that you wrote, they add the watermark anyway," Echols said...

Anthropic isn't the only AI lab to use watermarks: Google uses its SynthID technology to watermark AI-generated content, and OpenAI uses SynthID for supported images and audio. Elon Musk's social media platform X also adds a "Made with AI" tag on content it determines to be AI-generated or manipulated.


Long-time Slashdot reader kmleon (also a tech consultant and RPG researcher) experienced another issue. He'd built some software using their own custom-built AI tool, only asking Claude to do some testing. "Little did I know that Claude would sometimes decide, since it was involved on the edges... to take credit for all of my work, claiming some parts were either '100%' or 'Co-Authored/Created' by Claude.Ai / Claude Code!" I'm sure the good folks at Anthropic will eventually tweak Claude enough to, hopefully, not make these mistakes in the future.... I only became aware of it today, because I recently setup scanners to catch Claude incorrectly watermarking any content it touches for various projects I'm working on. I found that it has (apparently as far back as Sonnet 4.6, but as recently as today, August 14th, 2026) sometimes been mistakenly over-zealous in taking credit for 100% creating or co-authoring docs, code, images, videos, etc. I've only, so far, found about a dozen instances spanning the past year, and most of them appear to have been injected in the last few weeks, so it is not a common issue (yet).
On the bright side? Maybe watermarks can help AI stop training on AI-generated text.

Although Forbes also reports that Google "announced on Friday that it will now let users remove the visible watermark from AI-generated images, videos and music created with several of its models."

content_html_zh:
据博客 Futurism 报道，本周 Anthropic 宣布其 Claude 聊天机器人将为它生成的文本添加水印。 “它的工作原理是在人工智能生成的文本中对其词语选择进行微妙的改变，这些改变应该是人类无法察觉的，但总的来说，形成了一种可以用该工具检测到的模式。” Anthropic 表示，它正在实施水印系统，以响应欧盟 2024 年通过的具有里程碑意义的人工智能法案，该法案要求人工智能公司标记其系统生成或编辑的内容。 TechCrunch 指出，包括谷歌、Meta、微软、OpenAI 和 Synthesia 在内的其他公司已承诺遵守欧盟的准则。 但《福布斯》报道称，“有关克劳德水印的消息在 X 上引发了一场轩然大波，用户担心人工智能辅助写作现在将带有一种永久性的‘红字’。”（《福布斯》想知道媒体公司是否在使人工智能正常化，“同时对输出进行污名化”。）

但还有另一个问题。 《商业内幕》指出，Anthropic 表示水印表明克劳德处理过的文本，“并不一定是原作者。 该公司表示，克劳德校对、翻译、总结或以其他方式编辑内容后，标记可以保留...... 水印表明克劳德处理过文本，但不一定是它写的。”

在那之后的几天里，“自周一以来，已有数十人在 X 上发帖称，他们以水印为由取消了克劳德的订阅。” 捷克共和国的自由开发者 Vladislav Rajtmajer 告诉《商业内幕》，他周二取消了 Claude Max 订阅，称水印是主要原因。 他说，他使用人工智能进行代码审查和翻译，并担心发送给客户的代码上的人工智能标签可能会引发有关作者身份的问题或引发合同处罚…… 佐治亚州的人工智能顾问理查德·埃科尔斯(Richard Echols)也表示，他周三取消了克劳德·马克斯(Claude Max)的订阅，水印是他做出决定的一个主要因素。 他说，他使用克劳德为企业创建文档，并担心当他自己编写基础材料并仅使用聊天机器人进行编辑时，该标记可能会出现。 “即使你编辑自己写的作品，他们也会添加水印，”埃科尔斯说…… Anthropic 并不是唯一使用水印的 AI 实验室：Google 使用其 SynthID 技术为 AI 生成的内容添加水印，而 OpenAI 使用 SynthID 来支持图像和音频。 埃隆·马斯克的社交媒体平台 X 还在其确定由人工智能生成或操纵的内容上添加了“人工智能制造”标签。 Slashdot 的长期读者 kmleon（也是一名技术顾问和 RPG 研究员）遇到了另一个问题。 他使用自己定制的人工智能工具构建了一些软件，只要求克劳德做一些测试。 “我几乎不知道克劳德有时会做出决定，因为它涉及到边缘...... 声称我的所有工作都是由 Claude.Ai / Claude Code ‘100%’或‘共同创作/创建’的！” 我确信 Anthropic 的优秀人员最终会对克劳德进行足够的调整，希望将来不会再犯这些错误...... 我直到今天才意识到这一点，因为我最近设置了扫描仪来捕获克劳德错误地为我正在从事的各种项目所涉及的任何内容添加水印。 我发现它（显然可以追溯到 Sonnet 4.6，但就在今天，2026 年 8 月 14 日）有时会错误地过度热衷于 100% 创建或共同创作文档、代码、图像、视频等。到目前为止，我只发现了过去一年中的十几个实例，其中大多数似乎是在过去几周内注入的，因此这不是一个常见问题（还）。 好的一面？ 也许水印可以帮助人工智能停止对人工智能生成的文本进行训练。

尽管《福布斯》还报道称，谷歌“周五宣布，现在将允许用户从使用其多个模型创建的人工智能生成的图像、视频和音乐中删除可见水印。”
